patterns.comment: A comment line: an asterisk or a slash in the indicator area, column 7. The whole line is documentation; a slash also ejects the listing page. Every IBM i COBOL uses this reference format, so one set of column rules serves .cbl, .cbl38 and .cblle alike. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: comment.line.cobol.fixed

patterns.comment: A floating comment: *> opens one anywhere in the program-text area, either as a whole comment line or after a statement, and it runs to the end of the line. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: comment.line.cobol.floating

patterns.comment: The sequence number area, columns 1 through 6. The compiler does not require the numbers, and the characters may be anything, so the area is scoped like the RPG gutter rather than parsed. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: comment.gutter

patterns.comment: A continuation line carries a hyphen in the indicator area. The hyphen means the first nonblank character continues the previous line's last word or literal with no space between them. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: keyword.other.cobol.continuation

patterns.comment: A debugging line carries D in the indicator area and is compiled only WITH DEBUGGING MODE; the precompiler treats it as a comment. The marker is scoped and the rest of the line is left to the ordinary rules, the way the compiler itself reads it. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: keyword.other.cobol.debug

patterns.comment: The comment area, columns 73 through 80, which the reference gives over to the programmer. The look-ahead requires something to be there so a 72-character line does not open a block at the line break with nothing to close it.
patterns.name: comment.block.line.cobol.fixed

patterns.comment: An embedded SQL statement, which begins with EXEC SQL on one line and ends with END-EXEC. The period after END-EXEC belongs to COBOL, not to the statement. Source: IBM i 7.5 Embedded SQL programming, coding SQL statements in COBOL applications.
patterns.name: cobol.sql

patterns.comment: SQL's own comment, two hyphens to the end of the line, which is valid inside an embedded statement.
patterns.name: comment.line.cobol.sql

patterns.comment: A COBOL comment line inside an embedded statement: the reference allows * or / in the indicator area anywhere except between EXEC and SQL, and the precompiler reads a D debugging line as a comment too.
patterns.name: comment.line.cobol.fixed

patterns.comment: The sequence number area of a line inside an embedded statement, scoped as it is outside one.
patterns.name: comment.gutter

patterns.comment: A host variable: a colon and a COBOL data name, hyphens included, as in :MGR-NUM.
patterns.name: variable.parameter.cobol.sql

patterns.comment: A character literal in SQL, ended by the closing quote or the line end so an unclosed one cannot swallow the statement.
patterns.name: string.quoted.single.cobol.sql

patterns.comment: The reserved words of Db2 for i, the same list the RPGLE and RPG/400 grammars carry, kept identical so the three do not drift. Source: Reserved words, Db2 for i SQL reference.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.cobol.sql.reserved

patterns.comment: A number in an SQL statement.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.cobol.sql

patterns.comment: The ASSIGN clause's assignment-name, whose first part names the device: PRINTER, FORMATFILE, TAPEFILE, DISKETTE, DISK, DATABASE or WORKSTATION, joined by hyphens to the file name and optionally to the SI or ALWNULL attribute. The device and attribute are fixed vocabulary and are scoped; the file name between them is the programmer's and is not. Matched from the ASSIGN keyword so a data item named DISK-COUNT elsewhere is left alone. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539, ASSIGN clause, Table 7.

A conditional compilation directive, an IBM extension: >>DEFINE names a compilation variable, and >>IF, >>ELSE, >>END-IF, >>EVALUATE, >>WHEN and >>END-EVALUATE select the lines to compile by it. A directive must be specified entirely on one line, so the block ends at the line end. Written as a block so the words that exist only in this context are scoped only here. Longer names come first so END-EVALUATE is not read as END-IF's shorter cousin. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: cobol.directive

patterns.comment: The words that belong to directive syntax alone: AS and PARAMETER and OFF in a DEFINE, OVERRIDE to redefine a variable, and DEFINED in a constant conditional expression. OVERRIDE is one of Appendix E's flagged words and AS, DEFINED and PARAMETER are not reserved words at all, so none of them is scoped outside a directive line. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: keyword.control.cobol.directive

patterns.comment: The *CONTROL and *CBL compiler-directing statements, an IBM extension controlling the source listing. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: keyword.other.cobol.directing

patterns.comment: The PROCESS statement, which names compiler options ahead of the Identification Division and overrides the CRTCBLMOD and CRTBNDCBL parameters. Only the first line may carry the word PROCESS, but the options may continue over further lines, so the block runs to the separator period at a line end, or stops short of the Identification Division header if the period was left off. The options are scoped only inside the statement, because names such as DATE, JOB and OUTPUT are ordinary words elsewhere. Conflicting options are legal; the last one encountered takes precedence. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539, Appendix G.
patterns.name: cobol.process

patterns.comment: The allowable PROCESS statement options, the whole of Appendix G's tables: the OPTION flags and their NO forms, the conversion options, the listing options, and the parameter-style options such as GENLVL, FLAG, EXTDSPOPT and ARITHMETIC whose arguments follow in parentheses. Ordered longest-first so a NO form is not read as a prefix on the word it negates.
patterns.name: keyword.other.cobol.process.option

patterns.comment: The compiler-directing words that stand alone: EJECT, SKIP1, SKIP2, SKIP3 and TITLE control the listing. COPY and REPLACE are reserved words and are scoped by the keyword rule. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: keyword.other.cobol.directing

patterns.comment: A nonnumeric literal in quotation marks, with an X, B, N or G prefix making it hexadecimal, Boolean, national or DBCS. The match ends at the closing quote or at the line end, never beyond it: a literal that reaches column 72 unclosed is continued by a hyphen indicator line whose first nonblank character is a quotation mark, and that resumed piece is matched on its own line. Written as a match rather than a block so an unclosed quote cannot swallow the lines after it. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: string.quoted.double.cobol

patterns.comment: The same literal in apostrophes, which the compiler accepts with the APOST option. The prefixes and the line-end rule apply here too. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: string.quoted.single.cobol

patterns.comment: A PICTURE clause: the PIC or PICTURE keyword, an optional IS, and then the picture character-string, which is made of symbols such as 9 X A S V P Z and paired parentheses. The string is scoped as one span, because its characters mean nothing individually. A period ends the clause only when followed by a space or the line end, since a period inside the string is a decimal point. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.

The fields of the SQL communication area, which INCLUDE SQLCA defines and the precompiler fills: SQLCODE, SQLSTATE, the SQLERR fields, the warning flags, and the SQLCADE and SQLSTOTE redefinitions. A program tests them in ordinary COBOL code and names SQLCA itself inside EXEC SQL INCLUDE, so the rule is shared into both contexts. Ordered longest-first so SQLERRM does not take the front of SQLERRMC. Source: IBM i 7.5 Embedded SQL programming, SQLCA in COBOL.
patterns.name: variable.language.cobol.sql

patterns.comment: The figurative constants: ZERO, SPACE, HIGH-VALUE, LOW-VALUE, QUOTE and NULL with their plural spellings, and ALL. Ordered longest-first so ZERO does not take the front of ZEROES. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: constant.language.cobol.figurative

patterns.comment: The special registers, storage areas the compiler itself defines: RETURN-CODE, SORT-RETURN, WHEN-COMPILED, LINAGE-COUNTER, DEBUG-ITEM, DB-FORMAT-NAME and the XML registers. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: variable.language.cobol.register

patterns.comment: A level number at the start of Area A or B: 01 through 49 for group and elementary items, 66 for RENAMES, 77 for standalone items and 88 for condition names. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.cobol.level

patterns.comment: A numeric literal, with an optional sign and decimal point.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.cobol

patterns.comment: A division header, the four words that partition every program. They must begin in Area A. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
An intrinsic function: the word FUNCTION and one of the sixty function names the reference lists, LENGTH and TRIM and CURRENT-DATE among them. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.

Part of the ILE COBOL reserved word inventory, from Appendix E of the reference: the Standard COBOL words and the IBM extensions, split across several rules and ordered longest-first within each so WORKING-STORAGE matches before WORKING. The appendix's (2) and (3) words - reserved names the ILE compiler does not use - are left out, so a word this rule colours is one the compiler acts on. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: keyword.other.cobol

patterns.comment: Part of the ILE COBOL reserved word inventory, from Appendix E of the reference: the Standard COBOL words and the IBM extensions, split across several rules and ordered longest-first within each so WORKING-STORAGE matches before WORKING. The appendix's (2) and (3) words - reserved names the ILE compiler does not use - are left out, so a word this rule colours is one the compiler acts on. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: keyword.other.cobol

patterns.comment: Part of the ILE COBOL reserved word inventory, from Appendix E of the reference: the Standard COBOL words and the IBM extensions, split across several rules and ordered longest-first within each so WORKING-STORAGE matches before WORKING. The appendix's (2) and (3) words - reserved names the ILE compiler does not use - are left out, so a word this rule colours is one the compiler acts on. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: keyword.other.cobol

patterns.comment: Part of the ILE COBOL reserved word inventory, from Appendix E of the reference: the Standard COBOL words and the IBM extensions, split across several rules and ordered longest-first within each so WORKING-STORAGE matches before WORKING. The appendix's (2) and (3) words - reserved names the ILE compiler does not use - are left out, so a word this rule colours is one the compiler acts on. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: keyword.other.cobol

patterns.comment: The relational and arithmetic operator symbols. Two-character operators come first so <= is one token, and the minus stands alone only when clear of word characters, because the hyphen inside a name such as END-OF-FILE is part of the name. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.cobol

patterns.comment: A section header's name: a word beginning in Area A and followed by the word SECTION, an optional segment number and the separator period. The fixed section names, WORKING-STORAGE and FILE-CONTROL among them, are reserved words taken by the keyword rules first; what reaches this rule is a name the programmer chose, in the Environment or Procedure Division. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.cobol.section

patterns.comment: A paragraph or section name: a word beginning in Area A, column 8, followed by a separator period. The reserved word rules run first, so DECLARATIVES and the division headers are already taken by the time this is tried; what is left in Area A is a name the programmer chose. Source: ILE COBOL Language Reference SC09-2539.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.cobol.paragraph
